Phase 17 adds saved shopping-list persistence with CRUD endpoints and saved-list optimization reruns while storing only user input.

Phase 16.7 adds internal-only basket health diagnostics with deterministic alert thresholds over persisted basket analytics summaries.
Phase 16.7 exposes GET /analytics/basket-health for system monitoring without mutating analytics records or changing optimizer behavior.
Phase 16.6 adds opt-in persistent basket analytics records, aggregate basket summary helpers, and GET /analytics/basket-summary without changing optimizer behavior.
Basket analytics persistence is explicit, non-blocking on write failure, and stored in basket_analytics_store with malformed records ignored by aggregation.
Phase 16.5 adds a deterministic read-only basket quality metrics layer that reports resolver, pricing, optimization, and convenience metrics only when explicitly requested.
Phase 16.5 does not mutate inputs, persist analytics, call external services, use randomness, or change existing basket optimizer behavior.

Phase DB2.5 adds deterministic USDA food cluster candidate generation, candidate batch generation, inspection reports, materialization preview, cluster review, and ingredient nutrition mapping suggestions.
DB2.5 preserves the chain usda_foods -> usda_food_clusters/usda_food_cluster_candidates -> ingredient_nutrition_mappings -> ingredients and does not map raw USDA foods directly to Pricer ingredients.

DB2.5 ingredient nutrition mappings are sidecar-only reviewable suggestions from approved clusters; they do not publish nutrition to Firestore, call LLMs, cluster branded foods, or alter product/search/shopping/basket runtime behavior.

Phase DB2 adds a sidecar-only USDA/FoodData Central macro import into Postgres with normalized USDA tables, macro nutrient filtering, source-file metadata registration, import-run tracking, and fixture-based tests.

DB2 does not change Firestore runtime reads, kolkostruva.bg ingest, product search, shopping flows, basket logic, canonical products, ingredients, mobile app access, Open Food Facts import, recipe import, LLM calls, or app-facing nutrition publishing.
Phase DB1 adds a sidecar-only Postgres foundation with local compose support, connection helpers, migration tooling, health checks, and import metadata tables.
DB1 does not change product ingest, Firestore/flat-store runtime reads, product search, shopping flows, basket logic, canonical products, ingredients, or mobile app data access.

Phase DB0 documents the hybrid persistence architecture: Postgres should own future relational source truth, heavy imports, nutrition joins, source dedupe, and mapping-review staging while Firestore/flat store remains the active app-facing cache and user-state runtime.
DB0 is design-only; no code, migrations, dependencies, or data movement were introduced.

Phase 16.3 adds an optional basket explanation layer that turns single-store or multi-store optimizer output into app-ready English summaries, item notes, warnings, and limitations without changing optimizer behavior.
Phase 16.4 adds optional convenience-aware scoring that keeps product actual totals unchanged while adding effective totals, penalties, and before/after convenience recommendations.

Phase 16.2 adds a bounded multi-store basket optimizer that compares opt-in split baskets against the best single-store option and recommends multi-store only when savings, coverage, and score policy allow it.
Phase 16.1 adds a deterministic single-store basket optimizer and HTTP route that rank single-chain basket options with separate actual totals and internal penalty-based score totals.
Phase 16 source price values are treated as EUR; price lookup and basket optimization do not use BGN defaults, currency conversion, or exchange-rate APIs.

Phase 16.0 adds a deterministic canonical price-lookup layer and HTTP route that expose latest known prices, stale or missing status, best-price selection, and basket-plan price collection without mutating price history.
Phase 15.4 adds a deterministic basket-input planner and HTTP route that turn resolver output into ready, ambiguous, and unresolved planning buckets with explicit readiness and confirmation flags.

Phase 15.3 adds a read-only shopping-list resolution service and HTTP route that normalize messy item text, rank canonical candidates deterministically, and return resolved, ambiguous, or unresolved outputs for basket-ready downstream consumers.
Phase M0 adds a parallel meal-domain foundation with flat ingredient, hierarchy, unit, conversion, ingredient-rule, and product-to-ingredient bridge collections.
Phase M0 keeps ingredients separate from canonical retailer products and adds deterministic ingredient-level purchase conversion plus price-fallback projection.
Phase 6 adds streamed ZIP ingestion, scheduler-ready orchestration, analytics, alert detection, and pipeline logging.
Phase 6 now also reuses enrichment once per normalized source chain plus product code before writing per-store product records.

Phase 13 adds a deterministic cross-chain canonical product layer with flat canonical products, flat source-to-canonical mappings, canonical group samples, and warning logs for potentially risky merges.
Phase 13.5 tightens the canonical layer with explicit deterministic guards for stage, age-band, flavor, color, and pack-count mismatches.
Phase 13.6 adds deterministic numeric-range guards so slash-separated and hyphenated size-band variants stay separate unless their normalized ranges match.
Phase 13.7 adds deterministic year and age-statement guards so vintage years and aged expressions become explicit canonical variant boundaries.
Phase 13.8 adds deterministic volume and size guards so normalized ml, cl, l, g, and kg markers become explicit canonical variant boundaries while equivalent formats still merge.
Phase 13.9 adds deterministic numeric-family markers so count, age-band, and reserve-tier conflicts block merges while bare ambiguous numbers remain unresolved for later adjudication.

Phase 14.0 adds a durable canonical disambiguation queue, stable pair fingerprints, reusable decision records, and a dry-run-only unresolved-warning adjudication lane without changing live canonical merges yet.

Phase 14.1 adds an opt-in LLM adjudication runner that reads pending queue items, reuses cached decisions, validates model output strictly, persists valid decisions with provenance, and still does not mutate canonical products.
Phase 14.2 adds human review decisions, human-over-LLM effective decision precedence, reviewed_human queue status tracking, and summary metrics while still not mutating canonical products.

Phase 14.3 adds a controlled application layer that computes applied merge/block/skip/no-op views and audit logs from effective decisions without mutating canonical products, mappings, source identity, or deterministic grouping.

Phase 15 adds a strict additive canonical enrichment store keyed by canonical fingerprint, cache-first reuse, a controlled category hierarchy, optional LLM enrichment for net-new canonical products only, and strict schema validation plus normalization.

Phase 15.1 adds explicit canonical reader layer selections, deterministic enrichment-backed filters and search, lightweight enrichment analytics rollups, and intended live enrichment enablement by default runtime config while preserving non-fatal missing-key behavior.

Phase 15.2 adds bounded product-facing API handlers and HTTP routes for canonical product detail, search, enrichment-backed filter facets, and enrichment analytics summaries, with canonical_with_enrichment as the default consumer layer.
Phase 7 adds unmet-demand capture from zero-result queries and manual cant-find-this feedback, plus batch aggregation and clustering.
Phase 8 adds deterministic single-store and multi-store basket optimization on top of Phase 4 query results.
Phase 9 adds recurring watchlist detection, cooldown-aware nudges, significance flags, target-price handling, and daily summary generation.
Phase 10 adds backend entitlement records, RevenueCat-ready Flutter subscription flows, Firestore billing profiles, premium backend gating, and AdMob-ready wrappers.
Phase 11 audits deployment readiness across env vars, external services, native placeholders, and production blockers.
Phase 12 adds canonical search terms, synonym mapping, conservative typo correction, canonical query objects, and demand-log-driven synonym learning.
The mobile app still consumes the existing /query and /product/:id/history backend contracts without backend rewrites.
Repo-level Node verification still passes after the Phase 12 matcher changes.

The repo has deployable Firebase manifests and a vendored functions runtime, but it is still not production-ready by secrets alone because cloud rules, auth wiring, FCM registration, scheduler setup, and release credentials remain operator-owned.
Live Firebase, xAI, RevenueCat, AdMob, future Postgres credentials, deployed scheduling, mobile auth, FCM token capture, and store-release setup remain pending.
